observations: Three photos show a used car engine on a dirt ground, surrounded by other engine parts.
The engine has a black plastic cover with 'VVT-i' and the Toyota logo visible in photo 0 and photo 1.
The engine block is metallic and shows signs of rust and wear, especially on the intake manifold in photo 2.
Various hoses, wires, and components are attached, some appear frayed or disconnected.
The seller claims it is a 2010 Toyota Prado engine, 2TR VVT-i, 4-plugs.
No visible serial number or model tag is readable in any photo.
The watermark 'POSTED ON Jiji BLESSED CHILD' is overlaid on all photos.

claims.evidence: The 'VVT-i' and Toyota logo are visible on the cover in photo 0 and photo 1, supporting the brand and technology. The '2TR' model is not visible in any photo. The year 2010 and '4-plugs' cannot be verified from the photos.

risks.risk: Engine may not be from a 2010 Prado or may be from a different model/year
risks.proof: Photo of the engine block with visible casting number or VIN tag, or a photo of the vehicle it was removed from.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic 2TR engine, not a Prado-specific unit, which reduces value.

risks.risk: Engine may have internal damage or be non-functional
risks.proof: Video or photo of the engine running, or a close-up of the cylinder head, oil pan, and internal components to check for wear or damage.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working or with unknown condition, which reduces value.

risks.risk: Engine may be stolen or have title issues
risks.proof: Photo of the engine's serial number and matching vehicle registration or proof of legal ownership.
risks.if_unproven: Priced with a discount for potential legal risk, which reduces value.

proof_requests: Photo of the engine block with casting number or VIN tag.
Photo or video of the engine running.
Photo of the vehicle it was removed from, if available.
Proof of legal ownership or source of the engine.
response.reason: The engine is identified as a Toyota 2TR VVT-i by the visible cover, but the year, model (Prado), and condition cannot be verified from the photos. Hidden risks include incorrect model/year, internal damage, and legal issues. Without proof, the item cannot be priced accurately.
